newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan oil firms grapple with high product stocks.
newsitem.headline: Japan oil firms grapple with high product stocks.

text.p: High domestic stocks of gas oil and kerosene will be weighing heavily on the minds of Japan's oil refinery executives as they draft production and import plans for this fiscal year, oil industry sources say.
The high stockpiles could temper Japanese activity in Asian product markets this summer, they said.
Oil refiners must provide the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) with annual production and import plans around May, a month after the start of the fiscal year.
"I think the industry will want to put a cap on stock levels, to try to see that there isn't a further increase in (product) supply," a trader with a major oil company said.
Since late 1996, unseasonably mild winter temperatures have seen Japan's domestic stocks of refined products swell to levels some 20 percent higher than year-earlier levels.
Particularly conspicuous have been stockbuilds of kerosene and gas oil, which were soaring some 35 percent higher than levels a year earlier.
Industry sources say that imports, rather than refinery operating rates, will likely take the first hit.
"The first step traditionally is to cut imports. This is usually done before production is reduced," a trader with another major oil firm said.
He noted that as a general rule it is more cost efficient to buy crude oil and refine it in Japan than to import oil products from overseas.
Imports of kerosene in June 1996 were 127,000 kilolitres (kl) while imports of gas oil were 241,000 kl.
Together, that amounts to 77,000 barrels-per-day of kerosene and gas oil, a figure likely to wither this June in light of the high stock levels, oil industry sources said.
Japan typically imports from Singapore product markets, through Middle East term contracts, and more rarely, from South Korean refiners, traders said.
The latest government data shows that domestic stocks of oil products stood at 13.4 million kl at the end of March, a 19.3 percent rise from the comparable period in 1996.
Kerosene stocks for the same period amounted to about 2.4 million kl, up 37.4 percent from the end of March last year.
Gas oil stocks were roughly 2.2 million kl, up 34.9 percent year-on-year, according to the trade ministry statistics.
Kerosene and gas oil stocks at the end of March were larger than those during the comparable period over the last several years, traders say.
"These are indeed high stock figures," a source said.
Traders said refiners had stepped up kerosene imports and production last year ahead of the winter in order to match stock levels during the 1995/96 winter, but then were thwarted by the climate.
Maintenance checks could provide some relief for oil firms as low production could lead to a draw in stocks, traders said.
A number of Japanese companies have already closed, or are scheduled to close shortly for routine maintenance checks.

"Some of the stocks could be consumed during the period when refineries are going through maintenance closures, and this could bring the inventory down to last year's level," the industry source said.
